target_customer: Internal audit and SOX compliance teams at public companies, and their auditors
problem: Internal audit planning, control testing and workpaper documentation are manual and costly, and auditing talent is short.
business_model: Software-led audit service, described as 99 percent software and 1 percent services
product_category: AI financial audit and SOX compliance automation

founders.name: David Jin Li
prior_employers: MacroHive (financial research engineer, acquired by BGC)
founders.background_notes: Brothers. Top 13 in the UK Informatics Olympiad per YC page.

competitors.name: AuditBoard
competitors.what: Incumbent audit, risk and compliance platform that added AI features in 2025

technical_complexity.rationale: Agents must integrate with ERPs and audit tools and produce traceable workpapers; accuracy and audit trail demands raise difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Several AI audit startups launched around the same time, and the product works on top of existing systems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AuditBoard added AI capabilities in March 2025. No source shows an acquisition of Denki.

market_need_then: The company cites large audit spend and a talent shortage, which are unverified company claims. Public company SOX compliance is mandatory, which sustains demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Informal with emoji checkmarks; frames traditional audit as outdated and manual

brand_strength.rationale: Early stage; the name is a Japanese word for electricity but no source confirms the intent, and no brand press was found.

outcome_analysis: Denki, founded in 2025, raised a 4.1M seed in March 2026 co-led by Base10 and Shine Capital within months of the Fall 2025 batch. Founders with McKinsey and financial data pipeline experience fit the problem. Competing AI SOX startups raised similar money in the same period, so execution speed will decide the outcome.
notes: Seed confirmed by Crunchbase News and FinTech Global. Rivals Midship (seed Jan 2026) and Petual (Apr 2026) emerged after the batch start and are not listed as competitors at founding. Some listings place HQ in Sacramento vs San Francisco. The website fetch returned only a tagline. Outcome search found no negative news.
